md_linear_extension.blurb: Linear Extension is a single trailside boulder in the Henryton section of Patapsco Valley State Park, close to the Erebor boulders and a stream. It holds ten problems and nothing else: a couple of easy V1s, a middle band from V3 to V5, two V6s and one hard V8 line. The tallest problem tops out around twelve feet and the landing under it is fairly flat, so a single pad goes a long way. Expect a long, shared-use walk in along a river and rail line rather than a roadside stop, so it suits a dedicated half-day for strong boulderers more than a casual session.

md_waiting_on_a_train_area.blurb: Waiting On A Train is a small bouldering zone in Catoctin Mountain Park, up around 1,900 feet near the Hog Rock trail. Two mid-sized overhanging boulders form the core, with several lower vertical blocks strewn nearby. Ten problems span the whole range, from V0 up to V8: a few V2 and V3 problems, a pair of V4s, then a V5, a V7 and a V8 for the strong. The harder lines are the draw, and movement quality is praised across the grades. It sits a short bushwhack off the trail, so it feels quiet and wooded, and a couple of pads help on the overhangs.

md_the_gorge.blurb: The Gorge is a small pair of outcrops above Little Gunpowder Falls, reached from the Parkton end of the rail trail. The Whale is a lengthy slab facing east and only 30 to 40 feet high; The Squid is more blocky, with cracks on its southwest face. Ten routes, mostly trad with one top-rope, run from about 5.5 to 5.10, with most in the 5.7 to 5.8 range and cruxes usually near the ground. Pitches are short, around 25 to 35 feet. Expect lichen, moss and some mud, sharp but solid stone, and a rack of hexes and tricams rather than a sport setup.

md_eden_brook.blurb: Eden Brook is one small boulder beside a stream in Columbia, a neighborhood spot for a quick session rather than a destination. It stands about ten feet at its tallest and carries ten problems from V0 to V8, with most of the lines in the easy-to-moderate range and a couple of hard outliers. The stone is regarded as better than most in the area, with crimps and sidepulls on the arete lines and cracks around the back. It works for beginners and solo climbers; bring a pad or two, and be gentle with the loose flakes and vegetation on the less-developed side.

md_pinnacle.blurb: The Pinnacle is a detached spire about 50 feet tall at the south end of the King and Queen Seat in Rocks State Park, north of Baltimore. It holds ten routes, almost all trad with a few top-rope options, from around 5.4 up through the 5.11 range, so there is something for newer leaders and for stronger climbers alike. Several of its lines are among the most popular in the park. Bolts on top give anchors for rappel and top-rope setups. Reach it by walking down past the back of the main formation; the west-side lines need a third-class scramble up a gully.

md_biceps_wall.blurb: Biceps Wall sits behind and below the King and Queen Seat in Rocks State Park, on a south-facing section of cliff. It is the first area on the right when hiking in from the upper lot, which makes it handy when the main wall is busy. Ten routes, mostly trad and top-rope, run from easy 5.4 terrain through the 5.10s and 5.11s to one 5.12, with a good beginner-leader line among them. Anchors are usually rigged from the boulders behind the block above. Some climbs stay damp after heavy rain, and the stone can swallow small nuts while flaring placements make cams awkward.

md_hot_spot_boulder.blurb: Hot Spot Boulder is a steeply overhanging block, roughly 45 degrees, in the Fallston Boulder Garden, a shady and secluded patch of boulders. Ten problems give an unusual spread: five easy V0 to V1 lines, one V2, a trio at V5 and a single very hard V10-range line at the top end. The overhang makes the ground beneath it noticeably warmer than the surrounding woods, which makes it a popular pick for winter sessions. Expect steep, distinctive moves rather than slabs, and bring pads for the uneven ground. It lies just north of the Slumberous Hollow boulder.
